messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service runtime-prod /v1/generate p99 latency > 2s for last 5m. Error spike 502. Paging #eng-oncall. Thread TS=1704051234

oncall-maya: got the page, looking now. which region?

sre-anna: seeing elevated queue depth on runtime frontends in us-west-2; backend GPU workers also show high inflight (avg 28/32). error bursts map to customers using long-context LLM variants.

runtime-lead-sam: confirmed. KV cache hit rate fine. Kernel hot path CPU usage up on a subset of hosts. Feels like overload + queuing.

oncall-maya: initial mitigation idea: 1) apply tenant-level emergency rate limit to noisy customers, 2) reduce max_in_flight on frontends from 32 -> 16 to lower tail latency, 3) disable long-context variants temporarily. Any objections?

infra-joe: I'm ready to push config. rate limiter can do per-tenant burst window. can run via `trafficctl` or patch the rate-limiter configmap.

support-elaine: I have an open ticket from a large customer reporting 502s; if we throttle them we should coordinate. Can we do a targeted quota bump for their integration key temporarily?

pm-ryan: prefer preserve top customers if we can. If targeted quota helps them while shedding broad noise, do it. Keep me in the loop for comms.

runtime-lead-sam: plan: A) roll max_in_flight change to 16 on a small ring (10% hosts) as canary, B) enable probabilistic shedding after queue depth 50 with 20% shed rate, C) disable model_variant:long-context-2.1 across host pool, D) apply per-tenant rate cap for tenants with >200rps. If canary looks good, promote to full prod.

oncall-maya: can you post the exact commands?

runtime-lead-sam: sure:

```bash
# canary: change concurrency on ring-a
kubectl set env deployment/runtime-frontends -n prod MAX_IN_FLIGHT=16 --selector=ring=ring-a

# enable probabilistic shedding (traffic manager)
trafficctl set-shedding --service runtime-prod --threshold-queue 50 --probability 0.2 --env prod

# disable heavy model variant
modelsctl disable --model long-context-2.1 --env prod --reason "emergency shedding"

# per-tenant rate cap (example customer)
trafficctl set-rate --tenant customer-acme --service runtime-prod --rps 5 --duration 30m
```

oncall-maya: infra-joe will apply rate caps for top noisy tenants, runtime will roll canary. I'll monitor.

infra-joe: applying per-tenant caps now. doing customer-acme first.

incident-bot: Deploy started: kubectl set env deployment/runtime-frontends ring=ring-a by runtime-lead-sam at 1704051810

sre-anna: canary max_in_flight=16 rolled to ring-a (12 hosts). Observability: p95 improved from 1.8s -> 1.1s on ring-a, error rate down 40% there.

runtime-lead-sam: good. enabling probabilistic shedding on canary ring as well.

incident-bot: trafficctl set-shedding completed at 1704051955

oncall-maya: disable long-context variants now.

modelsctl: disabled long-context-2.1 across prod at 1704052002

support-elaine: customer-acme reports reduced errors after rate cap + small temporary key bump. I've applied a 2x quota bump for them for 1 hour.

pm-ryan: please log the customer bump with reason "mitigation - avoid critical customer outage" and follow up for compensation if needed.

infra-joe: I'm seeing overall drop in worker CPU contention after shedding; hosts reclaimed memory.

sre-anna: metrics summary 10m after canary: global p99 down 30%, overall 502s down 75%, but throughput down ~8% due to disabled long-context variant.

oncall-maya: decision: promote max_in_flight change to all rings. We'll keep probabilistic shedding global at p=0.2 and keep long-context disabled until tomorrow maintenance window.

runtime-lead-sam: promoting now.

incident-bot: Promotion started by runtime-lead-sam at 1704052510

sre-anna: promotion complete at 1704052630. observed immediate tail improvement. no regression alerts.

oncall-maya: customer impact summary for post-incident notes:
- Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate (primarily long-context models)
- Window: 1704051200 - 1704053000 (roughly)
- Severity: SEV2 (partial degradation; some 502s for heavy-model requests)
- Affected tenants: ~12 tenants had elevated errors; 3 tenants saw >20% errors; 1 enterprise (customer-acme) was close to outage but preserved via targeted bump.

support-elaine: I'll open proactive outreach for the three tenants with >20% errors.

pm-ryan: we'll send a short incident blurb to customers tomorrow with mitigation steps and ETA for re-enabling long-context variants.

oncall-maya: handoff: I'm handing off to night oncall (oncall-michael) at 1704054000 UTC. Things to watch: queue depth, p99 tail, model-variant re-enable ticket.

oncall-michael: taking handoff. please drop any runbook links.

oncall-maya: runbook link: https://console.internal/runbooks/runtime-backpressure (will pin in channel). Open items:
- revert long-context only after load-testing and grey rollout (ticket #3421)
- review client-side retry guidance (support)
- follow-up: adjust default max_in_flight config for long-term if pattern repeats

sre-anna: leaving postmortem notes: probable root cause = sudden spike of long-context greedy workloads + insufficient shedding in older config. Recommend: adaptive in-flight cap tied to tail latency, improved tenant-level noisy-neighbor detection.

pm-ryan: thanks team. label this for postmortem and cost/compensation review.

oncall-maya: closing the live thread; will file incident ticket and postmortem draft. re-open if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed by oncall-maya at 1704054567
